messages:
sam: FYI got a flurry of SCIM 422s after last night's IdP cert rotation. affected tenants report mass role removals. stack trace shows group attribute contains non-printable bytes.
kevin: can you paste a sanitized attribute payload?
sam: redacted excerpt from gateway logs:
```
<Attribute Name="groups">��gzipped: H4sI...==</Attribute>
<Attribute Name="role_hint">admin�</Attribute>
```
looks like a gzipped blob ended up inline and our CSV-splitter mis-parsed it.
ops: the IdP activity shows a cert rotate + a config tweak to send groups as a compressed attribute for large group sets. that change was supposed to be opt-in. not all tenants should have received it.
secbot: raising incident SEV-2. tagging infra and identity teams. also scanning vuln DB for any recent CVEs in the decompress libs.
kevin: KMS logs clear: no envelope/decrypt failures; this is pre-KMS (IdP -> gateway) text munging.
lina: root cause hypothesis: identity-gateway expects plain UTF-8 XML attributes and treats any non-ascii as bad. with compressed payload the gateway didn't strip compression marker and downstream SCIM CSV parser saw binary characters -> group parsing failed -> role mappings returned empty -> RBAC engine removed roles.
ops: i can repro locally by taking a group array, compressing with gzip, base64ing and embedding in Attribute value. gateway receives base64, decodes, but does not detect gzip magic (0x1f8b) before handing to XML parser. parser then yields weird_control_chars.
kevin: quick mitigation suggestions:
- gate the new IdP opt-in: ask IdP team to stop sending compressed attributes for our tenants until gateway supports it
- emergency patch to identity-gateway: detect gzip magic bytes after base64 decode and inflate before parsing
- add a defensive SCIM validation step that rejects provisioning requests where groups field is non-UTF8 printable and returns a clear error to IdP
secbot: also add an audit flag on any provisioning event that changes role set because of malformed attributes: "audit_malformed_attr":"true". export these to sec-analytics and file an automated ticket in support queue.
sam: ops, can you put the WAF rule to block base64 payloads that decode to gzipped content for 30m as a temporary measure (alert-only mode)?
ops: WAF rule in alert-only now. no false positives yet.
kevin: i've opened a small PR to detect gzip magic and inflate in the gateway. will add metrics and a feature flag. tag: deploy-bot will run canary.
deploy-bot: identity-gateway v3.2.1-canary deployed at 2026-03-22T05:40Z to canary cluster. monitoring for errors.
lina: starting RBAC reconcile job for ent tenants affected. if we can capture attribute hashes + timestamp window we can backfill role changes. need 12h audit logs.
secbot: scheduled vuln triage: check zlib/gzip CVEs and ensure we're using safe inflate APIs (no zip-slip / decompression bombs). add rate limits on decompression.
kevin: mitigation checklist:
- short: block compressed attrs at WAF + request IdP rollback for non-opted tenants
- mid: gateway patch with charset and compression autodetect + metrics + structured audit fields
- long: add schema version negotiation for SAML attributes and document compression opt-in in onboarding docs
sam: canary shows errors drop to near-zero after patch. requesting prod rollout in 40m with rollback plan.
ops: prod deploy scheduled +40. will post status.
lina: postmortem owners: lina (RBAC reconcile), kevin (gateway fix), sam (incident lead), ops (deploy), secbot (vuln triage).
secbot: record for compliance: any provisioning change that removed roles must have an audit trail and a ticket opened for every impacted user. recommend 90-day retention for these specific audit entries.
kevin: opened GH issue linking PR, incident notes, and follow-ups. will include a unit test covering gzip-detection and a fuzzer for malformed attr payloads.
sam: thanks all. next steps: continue reconcile, review audit exports, finalize postmortem with timeline and contribute to onboarding docs so IdP teams don't flip opt-ins without speaking to us. closing here once prod deploy is green. :rocket:
